title: Kailash Mansarovar Yatra Cost via Nepal
meta_description: Kailash Mansarovar yatra cost via Nepal by route: Kerung overland, Simikot heli, Lhasa fly-in and private charter, what is included, extras and visa fees.
summary: A Kailash Mansarovar yatra via Nepal costs roughly ₹1,90,000–2,60,000 per person overland via Kerung, ₹2,60,000–3,60,000 via Simikot by helicopter and ₹3,00,000–3,80,000 with a Lhasa fly-in, twin sharing. Ponies, porters, visa fees, insurance and tips are usually extra. Fees for Indian passport holders change; check current status.

sections.heading: What a Kailash yatra costs by route
paras: The single biggest factor in the price is the route. Overland via the Rasuwagadhi–Kyirong border has been the cheapest way from Nepal because it uses only road transport; the Simikot route adds two domestic flights and a helicopter sector; and the Lhasa route adds international flights to and from Lhasa and several extra nights in Tibet. A private helicopter charter sits at the top of the range.

The figures below are indicative per-person prices for a group of about 10, twin sharing, in a standard season, as quoted by commercial agencies including ours. Prices for Indian passport holders have sometimes differed from those for other nationalities, and the Kerung route was closed by floods in August 2026, so check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Where the money goes
paras: Most of a yatra price is spent inside Tibet, where all services must be bought from licensed Tibetan agencies. The Tibet side covers the Tibet Travel Permit and area permits, a licensed guide for the whole stay, vehicles and drivers, eco-bus tickets at Manasarovar and the kora, accommodation from the border onwards and, in our groups, a cook and support crew preparing Indian vegetarian food. On a typical overland yatra this accounts for well over half of the total.

On the Nepal side, the price covers hotels in Kathmandu or Nepalgunj, transfers, the Nepali tour leader, and on the heli route the flights to Nepalgunj and Simikot plus the helicopter sector to Hilsa. Helicopter costs are shared across the group at four or five passengers per sortie, so smaller groups or lighter loads raise the per-person price.

Finally there is equipment and safety: oxygen cylinders, a pulse oximeter, a first-aid kit and loaned down jackets and duffels. Packages that look very cheap often leave out the cook, the oxygen or the Nepali leader, or use the most basic rooms.
list: Tibet ground services and permits: roughly 50–65% of the price
Nepal hotels, transfers and leader: roughly 10–15%
Safety equipment, loaned gear and agency costs: the remainder

sections.heading: Visa and permit fees
paras: Every pilgrim needs a Chinese group visa and the Tibet Travel Permit with additional area permits for Ngari. The permits are obtained by the Tibetan agency and included in package prices. The group visa fee depends on nationality and on whether express processing is needed, and agencies usually list it separately because it changes.

For Indian passport holders on the Nepal routes, the visa process, biometric requirements and fees have changed several times since 2023. In recent seasons resident Indians have had their visas processed through the Chinese embassy in New Delhi, with original passports submitted weeks before departure, and some seasons have carried charges specific to Indian nationals. Ask your agency for the current figure in writing, and check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Extras not in the package price
paras: Budget for these on top of the package. The pony and porter rates are set by the local cooperative in Darchen each season and paid in Chinese yuan, so treat the figures as approximate.
list: Pony with horseman for the 3-day parikrama: about US$ 450–550
Porter for the 3-day parikrama: about US$ 180–250
Tips for the Tibetan guide, drivers and cook: about ₹3,000–5,000 per pilgrim in total
Tips for Nepali staff, horsemen and porters: as you see fit, usually a day's hire for horsemen
Travel insurance covering altitudes up to 6,000 m and helicopter evacuation
Extra nights caused by weather, landslides or border delays, charged at cost
Personal spending: drinks, snacks, phone, laundry and gifts

sections.heading: Why quotes differ between agencies
paras: Two quotes for the same route can differ by ₹40,000 or more. The usual reasons are group size, since permits, guide and vehicles are shared; hotel category in Kathmandu and on the Tibet side; whether meals are cooked by the agency's crew or bought at roadside restaurants; and whether oxygen, loaned gear and a Nepali leader are included.

On the heli route, check how many passengers are planned per helicopter sortie and whether the price covers one waiting day in Simikot. On the overland route, check whether the Darchen night after the parikrama is included or whether the group drives straight to Saga. And always check which nationality the price is for, because rules and fees for Indian nationals have differed.

sections.heading: How to keep the cost down safely
paras: The most effective way to save is to join a fixed-departure group of 10 or more, which spreads permits, vehicles and the helicopter across more people. Avoid the Saga Dawa week if you do not need it, because accommodation and services carry a premium. Book early so you can choose the route rather than take whatever has seats.

Do not save on acclimatisation days, oxygen or insurance. An itinerary that cuts a night in Kyirong or Purang to shave the price can turn a yatra into a medical emergency at 5,000 m. Similarly, a pony booked in advance costs less than an evacuation from Dirapuk.

sections.heading: The official government yatra
paras: The Government of India's Kailash Mansarovar Yatra via the Lipulekh pass in Uttarakhand and Nathu La in Sikkim is a separate scheme run by the Ministry of External Affairs. It resumed in 2025 after a break of several years, with applicants chosen by a computerised draw and costs set by the government each year. It takes longer than the Nepal routes and has its own eligibility rules, including an age range of 18 to 70.

Many pilgrims apply for both: if they are not selected in the draw, they book a Nepal-route yatra instead. The two schemes do not affect each other, but you cannot hold travel dates on both at once. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What is the total cost of Kailash Mansarovar yatra from India via Nepal?
faqs.a: Allow about ₹2,10,000–3,00,000 per person for the package, depending on route, plus ₹40,000–80,000 for flights or travel to Kathmandu or Nepalgunj, visa fees, a pony and porter, insurance and tips. The Simikot heli route costs more than the overland Kerung route; the Lhasa route costs most.

faqs.q: What is the cheapest way to do Kailash yatra from Nepal?
faqs.a: The overland route via Kerung in a fixed-departure group has been the cheapest, from about ₹1,90,000. It was closed by floods in August 2026, so check current status before you travel. When it is closed, the Simikot heli route in a large group is usually the next most economical.

faqs.q: Why is the helicopter Kailash yatra more expensive?
faqs.a: It adds Kathmandu–Nepalgunj and Nepalgunj–Simikot flights and the Simikot–Hilsa helicopter sector, which is shared by only four or five passengers per sortie. Weather delays can also add hotel nights. In return, it saves several long driving days.

faqs.q: Is the Kailash yatra cost different for Indians and foreigners?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Indian passport holders have faced different visa processing, biometric rules and, in some seasons, nationality-specific charges on the Nepal routes. Foreigners pay their own nationality's visa fee. Ask for a quote for your exact passport, and check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Does the Kailash yatra price include the pony?
faqs.a: Usually not. Ponies and porters are hired through the local cooperative at Darchen at rates set each season, and paid in yuan. A pony with horseman for three days has cost roughly US$ 450–550 and a porter roughly US$ 180–250. Your guide books them for you.

faqs.q: How much should I tip on a Kailash yatra?
faqs.a: Our groups usually give the Tibetan guide, drivers and cook about ₹3,000–5,000 per pilgrim in total, horsemen and porters roughly one day's hire for the three-day kora, and Nepali staff according to service. Tips are voluntary but customary.

faqs.q: Is travel insurance included in Kailash packages?
faqs.a: Rarely. You must buy a policy that covers trekking up to about 6,000 m, emergency evacuation including helicopter, and medical treatment abroad. Check age limits on the policy, because some insurers restrict cover for travellers over 70.

faqs.q: How much does a Mansarovar-only yatra cost?
faqs.a: A Mansarovar yatra without the parikrama via Simikot costs about ₹2,20,000–2,80,000 per person. Our 9-day version starts from ₹2,45,000. It saves the pony and porter costs and two nights on the kora but uses the same flights, helicopter and permits.

faqs.q: When should I pay for a Kailash yatra?
faqs.a: Agencies usually take a deposit at booking and the balance about 45–60 days before departure, when Tibet permits are applied for. Ask for the cancellation terms in writing, including what is refunded if permits are refused or the border closes.
